BLOCKER: **Acceptance criterion not objectively met.** The AC requires an *in-process API (B)* for the review tool plus *PF server/service SSOT* wiring. `PF-API-SERVICE-OR-SERVER.md` is pre-existing (appears as a context line in `gen_docs_index.py`) and unchanged by this diff. The only "wiring" shipped is a script-local `_item_dispositions()` that reaches directly into the item store via `_get_item()` — i.e., the review tool bypasses any API/contract layer and reads a free-form dict. No API surface, no schema, no server/service change is in the diff; four of the five changed files are process docs and generated artifacts. Gate 1.5/2.5 are not "wired fully."
MAJOR: **Disposition integrity: ordinal-keyed dispositions silently misattribute.** Findings are numbered by enumeration order (`for sev in SEVERITIES: for text in f.get(sev,[])`, key = `str(n)`). A re-review (Gate 2.5 re-run after new commits) that adds/removes/reorders findings silently re-points every stored disposition at a different finding, with no warning, no content hash, and no supersession check. This directly risks the exact "silent divergence" the new `CORRECTION-LEDGER.md`/`MODEL-ASSISTED-ENGINEERING.md` docs declare as the enemy. Findings need a stable identity (e.g., content hash) before dispositions are keyed to them.

**Duplicated review renderers will drift.** `_render_review()` is added while the existing `review_block()` (previously used on this exact path, and presumably still used elsewhere, e.g. `emit`) is left in place. Two renderers for the same review view violate the reuse/single-writer principle the diff itself codifies; the legacy path will show findings without dispositions and quietly re-introduce the split view this item is meant to eliminate.

**Fail-open on read errors contradicts the repo's own fail-closed standard.** `_item_dispositions()` swallows all exceptions and returns `{}`, so a broken/unreadable item renders every finding as "(no response yet)" / PENDING-looking state rather than erroring. The new SSOT docs define "fail-closed: unknown/missing evidence ⇒ blocked"; the implementation of that very gate does the opposite. An unreadable item must surface loudly (or block), not degrade to an empty response set.

**Self-declared "SSOT 100%" maturity is false and contradicts the doc's own rule.** All four new docs are registered as `("SSOT", ..., 100)` in `gen_docs_index.py`/README/HTML, yet `CORRECTION-LEDGER.md` CL-001 explicitly says its enforcement is "ownership gate (pending)" and CL-002's enforcement is only partially implemented by this diff. The ledger's own rule — "if it isn't enforced somewhere machine-readable, it isn't fixed" — makes these docs, by their own standard, *not done*. Marking aspirational process docs as 100%-adopted SSOT is exactly the "verification optimism / self-report as evidence" failure mode §2.5 of MODEL-ASSISTED-ENGINEERING.md describes.

**Free-form `review_dispositions` write path with no schema or validation.** Adding the field name to `_CONTEXT_FIELDS` lets the operator-guarded context POST accept an arbitrary dict (unknown statuses, wrong key format, dispositions for findings that don't exist). Given this becomes an indexed RAG source (`RAG-PROCESS-MEMORY.md` §2/§4) and a Gate 2 precondition ("all dispositions non-PENDING"), an unvalidated shape will corrupt downstream gates and retrieval. Needs a schema (statuses enum, key format) and validation at the write path — the single-writer store, not the reviewer tool.
MINOR: **Dead/confused fallback logic in `_item_dispositions`.** `d.get(mode) or d.get("design" if mode == "design" else "diff")` — when `mode == "design"` the fallback is identical to `d.get(mode)`; the branch is a no-op, indicating unresolved gate/mode vocabulary (`--gate 1|2` vs `mode design|diff`). Pin the vocabulary in `GLOSSARY.md` (which this diff creates) and use one enum consistently.

**Test-run id-block reservations committed into the shared allocator SSOT.** `id-blocks.json` churn (`_test_staleness`, `_test_lease_gate`, `reserved_up_to` bumps) mixes ephemeral test-session state into a repo-tracked single-source-of-truth config. If test allocations must persist, they belong in test-scoped storage, not the production SSOT file — otherwise concurrent real sessions and test noise contend on one file (merge conflicts, allocator drift).

**`BACKLOG-SUMMARY.md` shows Must item BI-PF-1430 disappearing** from the tracked section (replaced by BI-PF-1431) with no trace of disposition in this diff. Generated file, so likely correct upstream, but a Must item silently vanishing from the summary warrants an explicit closure/renumber note for auditability.

Four new top-level `docs/*.md` SSOT files plus README + HTML index edits in a single item is heavy doc-topology churn; consider whether glossary/process guardrails deserve their own tracked backlog items (they are described as multi-item epics in §8 of MODEL-ASSISTED-ENGINEERING.md).
SUMMARY: The diff does not deliver the stated AC: there is no in-process API (B) and no PF server/service SSOT change — the reviewer tool reads item context directly, and the bulk of the diff is process documentation self-labeled "SSOT 100%" while its own text admits enforcement is pending. The one concrete wiring (dispositions rendering) has a serious integrity flaw — dispositions keyed by unstable ordinal finding numbers, which will silently misattribute on re-review — plus a fail-open error path and an unvalidated free-form write schema for what is intended to become a Gate 2 gate and a RAG-indexed source of truth. Top risks: (1) AC shortfall / doc-as-deliverable substitution, (2) disposition misattribution on re-review, (3) unvalidated `review_dispositions` propagating into gates and retrieval.
